bottleneck_name: Target validation / translational validity of target biology
current_state_metric: Share of all clinical failures attributed to lack of efficacy
trend_rate: Efficacy remains the largest failure class across 2015 and 2024 reviews; in-house replication rates of published target claims 11% (Amgen) and ~33% (Bayer) show no documented improvement
direct_constraint_evidence: Acts on the largest single attrition mass (40-50% of failures). Input quality is measurably poor: 6 of 53 landmark oncology papers replicated; two-thirds of Bayer validation projects inconsistent. No spare-capacity counter-evidence exists because target choice is not a capacity resource - it is a selection quality variable, so marginal return is not capped by parallelisation.
elasticity_basis: eps_P = 10 x ((1-PoS)/PoS) x f x theta; PoS=0.12, f=0.45, theta=0.15-0.45. Derived record E-3081.
modality_variance: Binds hardest where target biology is the whole bet: small molecule and antibody programs in CNS, immunology and metabolic disease. Binds least for vaccines (antigen validity is often known) and for cell therapy in haematology (CD19/BCMA targets already clinically validated). ADC inherits target risk from the antibody plus payload-window risk. RNA and gene therapy in monogenic disease have the lowest target risk because human genetics supplies the validation.
region_variance: Low region sensitivity; target selection is globally shared literature. China-origin programs are disproportionately fast-follower on validated targets, which lowers B1 exposure but raises commercial crowding.
notes: Highest elasticity but lowest controllability: a 10% improvement in target validity is far harder to purchase than a 10% increase in capital. Rank reflects elasticity per M2, not tractability.

bottleneck_name: Preclinical-to-clinical translation (animal model predictivity, NAM validation)
current_state_metric: Fully qualified drug development tools under FDA ISTAND
trend_rate: From no formal NAM pathway pre-2022 to FDA Modernization Act 2.0/3.0, an April 2025 FDA roadmap, and the first organ-chip reaching final qualification stage by early 2026; still zero completed qualifications
direct_constraint_evidence: Constraint is the supply of validated replacement methods, not sponsor willingness: 16 ISTAND projects have produced no qualified tool. Natural experiment available in ALS, where >100 compounds active in the mouse model showed no effect on retest and 8 had already failed in patients - relaxing reliance on that model would have prevented those trials.
elasticity_basis: eps_P with f=0.25, theta=0.10-0.35 (theta capped low by zero qualified NAMs), plus eps_C ~0.3. Derived record E-3082.
modality_variance: Binds hardest on small molecules and ADCs, where rodent and NHP tox studies are the gate. Binds moderately on antibodies, where species cross-reactivity often forces NHP-only tox and FDA has named mAbs as the first phase-down target. Binds least on cell and gene therapy, where animal models are already acknowledged as weakly predictive and regulators accept mechanistic and ex vivo human data. Vaccines sit in between (challenge models).
region_variance: US moving fastest on NAM acceptance (FDA roadmap, FDAMA 3.0). EU driven by REACH/3Rs but slower on drug-specific qualification. CN and JP-KR largely follow ICH; NAM-only packages face higher rejection risk outside the US, so global programs must still run the animal package.
notes: The widely quoted 90-95% animal-to-human failure figure is advocacy-sourced with no disclosed denominator; treated here as unverified and not used in the elasticity calculation.

bottleneck_name: Clinical trial patient recruitment / site capacity
current_state_metric: Activated investigative sites that under-enrol or enrol nobody
trend_rate: Enrollment interval lengthened 36.9% between 2010 and 2020; industry-to-federal oncology enrollment ratio doubled from 4.8 to 9.6 between 2008-2012 and 2018-2022
direct_constraint_evidence: Strong queueing evidence: 1 in 10 sites enrol zero patients, 48% under-enrol, over 80% of trials miss the enrollment timeline, and Phase III conduct burns $55,716 per day so the queue is priced. IMPORTANT counter-nuance: the raw patient pool is NOT at capacity - only about 7% of cancer patients enter any study and 56% of non-enrollment is because no suitable trial exists at the patient's site. The binding sub-resource is activated, matched site capacity, not patients.
elasticity_basis: eps_C (c=0.30-0.40, tau=0.5-0.7, delta=0.6) plus enrollment-failure rescue term (rho=0.03-0.08) times a 1.3-1.6 queueing multiplier. Derived record E-3083.
modality_variance: Binds hardest on cell and gene therapy (tiny eligible pools, few qualified treatment centres, apheresis and ICU infrastructure required) and on rare-disease RNA/gene programs. Binds moderately on oncology small molecule/ADC/antibody in biomarker-selected settings. Binds least on vaccines and on large common-disease small molecule programs, where site networks are deep and enrollment is fast.
region_variance: US site productivity is the weakest per-site and the most expensive; EU is slower to activate but more consistent per site; CN can enrol oncology trials several times faster at large centres, which is why sponsors increasingly run first-in-human in China; JP-KR sit between EU and CN with strong per-site quality but small pools.
notes: Most-complained-about bottleneck in the industry, but its elasticity is mid-pack because it acts mainly on cost and schedule, not on probability of success. Do not conflate its visibility with its marginal return.

current_state_metric: Patients screened per enrolled participant in biomarker-selected trials
unit: ratio (2,500 HLA screens per ~38 enrollees, one cell therapy trial)
trend_rate: Subpopulation-restricted approvals have risen over the past decade to nearly match all-comer approvals, and reach market demonstrably later
direct_constraint_evidence: Screening burden is documented (NCI-MATCH screened ~6,000 patients with a 143-gene panel to fill ~40 arms). But the constraint is bidirectional: enrichment raises PoS while shrinking the pool, so 'improvement' must be defined as screening efficiency, not as less precision. No evidence found that relaxing biomarker selection raises system output; the available evidence points the other way.
elasticity_basis: eps_C on screening cost (c=0.15, tau=0.6, delta=0.6) plus schedule pass-through via B3. Sign flips negative if 'improvement' means looser eligibility. Derived record E-3084.
modality_variance: Binds hardest on cell therapy (HLA plus antigen plus fitness selection stacks multiplicatively) and on gene therapy for ultra-rare monogenic disease where the global pool can be under 1,000 patients. Binds strongly on ADC and targeted small molecules in oncology. Binds weakly on antibodies in broad immunology indications and negligibly on vaccines.
region_variance: CN has the largest single-country pools for common oncology biomarkers and the fastest accrual; US pools are fragmented across many competing trials; EU fragmentation is regulatory and linguistic as much as biological; JP-KR pools are small enough that ultra-rare precision trials are frequently infeasible domestically.
notes: Frequently described as a bottleneck, but it is largely a chosen trade that buys probability of success. Ranked low deliberately.

bottleneck_name: Regulatory review capacity and evidence standards (incl. AI/NAM evidence acceptance)
current_state_metric: On-time completion of FDA approval actions
trend_rate: 46 CDER novel approvals in 2025 and nearly all PDUFA commitments met despite ~3,500 staff terminated in April 2025; on-time rate slipped roughly 8-12 points in H2 2025
direct_constraint_evidence: NEGATIVE finding - the US review step has demonstrable spare capacity. Output held at 46-53 novel approvals through a 3,500-person workforce reduction, which is a natural experiment in the wrong direction: capacity was cut hard and throughput barely moved. Review also occupies roughly 10-12 months of a 9.1-year clinical span, capping any achievable gain. Where B5 does bind is evidence standards, not headcount: only 11 biomarkers and zero organ chips have completed qualification.
elasticity_basis: eps_C with c=0.03, tau=0.5, delta=0.6 gives 0.09; remainder is an evidence-standard term better attributed to B2 and B15. Derived record E-3085.
modality_variance: Binds hardest on cell and gene therapy and on ADCs, where CMC review and inspection cycles dominate and where OTP/CBER capacity is thinner than CDER's. Binds least on small molecules and antibodies with conventional packages. Vaccines are region-politically sensitive rather than capacity-limited.
region_variance: US: not capacity-binding. EU: centralised procedure adds months but is predictable. CN: median ICI indication lag of 344 days behind FDA versus 118.5 days for the EU - materially binding for patient access though not for global approval count; rare-disease lag has compressed to ~1.4 years. JP-KR: PMDA and MFDS impose local-data expectations that add a development leg rather than review time.
notes: This is the clearest 'widely assumed bottleneck with spare capacity' finding in the set. Rank 14 on capacity grounds; the evidence-standards component is re-scored separately as B15.

bottleneck_name: CMC / manufacturing (viral vector, plasmid, LNP, ADC conjugation, aseptic fill-finish, autologous cell therapy)
current_state_metric: Candidates securing a commercial autologous CAR-T manufacturing slot
trend_rate: Viral vector suite capacity now modelled to exceed demand through 2031 (clinical demand CAGR ~4%); simultaneously CDMO consolidation removed six of ten Resilience sites in 2025 and ADC conjugation and fill-finish remain tight
direct_constraint_evidence: Textbook constraint for autologous cell therapy: explicit rationing (40% of eligible patients got no slot), 25% manufacturing failure in NHL, 5-8 week vein-to-vein, and documented waitlist progression and mortality. This is queueing with measured loss. Equally clear NEGATIVE finding for AAV suite capacity: independent modelling projects supply outpacing demand through 2031, so the AAV constraint is yield and cost per dose (up to 1e14 vg per patient), not suite count. Small molecule and mAb manufacturing show no queueing evidence at all.
elasticity_basis: Segment-weighted: cell/gene ~12.5% of programs at segment elasticity 15-40 (point 25), discounted 0.4-0.6 for the share accruing to commercial supply rather than approvals, band widened for ADC. Derived record E-3086.
modality_variance: LARGEST modality spread of any candidate. Autologous cell therapy: elasticity 15-40% (point 25) - the binding constraint for that modality. ADC: 3-8% (payload precursor, ADC-specific fill-finish lines, bioconjugation chemists; >200 candidates and 41 in Phase III chasing the same suites). Gene therapy/AAV: 2-6% but expressed as cost per dose, not capacity. RNA/LNP: 1-3%, post-COVID capacity ample. Antibody: 0.5-2%, titres and single-use capacity have outrun demand. Small molecule: ~0-0.5%, effectively unconstrained. Vaccine: 0.5-2% outside pandemic surge.
region_variance: US and EU carry most GMP cell therapy capacity but also the tightest qualified-personnel constraint. CN has the largest and cheapest vector and ADC capacity but faces geopolitical de-risking (WuXi divested its US/UK advanced therapies unit), which raises effective cost for Western sponsors. JP-KR are net importers of CGT manufacturing with growing domestic ADC and biologics capacity.
notes: Ranked 9 at whole-system level and rank 1 for autologous cell therapy. Reporting a single system rank for B6 would misrepresent it - the M5 decomposition is the finding.

bottleneck_name: Delivery and biodistribution (extrahepatic delivery, BBB, solid-tumour penetration)
current_state_metric: Injected dose reaching brain with an engineered peptide-conjugated LNP
trend_rate: From effectively liver-only systemic RNA delivery in the mid-2010s to demonstrated single-digit-percent CNS and muscle delivery and 6.7-10 fold enhancement with physical adjuncts
direct_constraint_evidence: Acts as a feasibility gate rather than a queue: hepatic accumulation is described as the central obstacle for extrahepatic nucleic acid therapeutics, and ultrasound-assisted delivery raising brain LNP signal 10-fold shows that delivery, not payload design, is the limiting variable in those models. No natural experiment at system scale has occurred, so the marginal-output link is inferential, and the elasticity band is correspondingly wide.
elasticity_basis: eps_P with f=0.15, theta=0.10-0.40, plus an option-value term up to 1.6 for indications currently outside the feasible set. Explicitly wide band. Derived record E-3087.
modality_variance: Binds hardest on RNA (siRNA/ASO/mRNA) and gene therapy, where tissue tropism determines which diseases are addressable at all. Binds hard on ADC and antibody in solid tumours (penetration gradients) and on any CNS indication. Binds least on small molecules, which are the incumbent solution to delivery, and on vaccines, where the delivery target is the immune system itself. Cell therapy faces a distinct version - trafficking into solid tumours rather than crossing barriers.
region_variance: Not region-sensitive; this is a physics and biology constraint. Regional variation appears only in tolerance for invasive delivery routes in trials.
notes: Tied at rank 5 with B15. Ranked on option value: it does not slow existing programs, it deletes indication classes from the addressable set, which is the larger long-run effect on approvals.

current_state_metric: Share of clinical failures attributed to uncontrollable toxicity
trend_rate: Safety and toxicology were the largest attrition source across four companies for 2000-2010 and toxicity still carries ~30% of failures in 2024 reviews; no measurable improvement despite two decades of in silico tox investment
direct_constraint_evidence: Second-largest attrition mass, and unlike efficacy failure it is largely predictable in principle. Marginal-return evidence: toxicity drives roughly two-thirds of post-launch withdrawals, so each prevented late failure returns both the trial cost and the launched-asset value. Skysona's 15% malignancy rate in trial participants shows the failure mode persists in the newest modalities. Not parallelisable - a tox signal terminates the program regardless of how much capacity is available.
elasticity_basis: eps_P with f=0.30, theta=0.15-0.40, plus a late-stage avoided-spend term. Derived record E-3088.
modality_variance: Binds hardest on small molecules (off-target, DILI, hERG) and ADCs (payload-driven ocular, haematologic and interstitial lung toxicity is the dominant ADC failure mode). Binds hard on gene therapy through insertional mutagenesis and complement activation, and on cell therapy through CRS/ICANS and secondary malignancy. Binds moderately on antibodies (immunogenicity, cytokine effects) and on RNA (innate immune activation, hepatotoxicity at dose). Vaccines carry rare but reputationally decisive safety risk.
region_variance: Low region sensitivity in the biology. Regulatory tolerance differs at the margin: FDA has been more willing than EMA to accept managed risk in oncology, and CN accepts higher CAR-T toxicity thresholds in relapsed settings.
notes: Tied on elasticity point with B11 at 6.0. Ranked 2 rather than 3 because it acts on probability of success, which is the axis with the weakest existing tooling, whereas the capital channel already has functioning markets.

current_state_metric: Unfilled requests for research non-human primates at US National Primate Research Centers
trend_rate: Automated platforms now report thousands of samples per day against roughly ten reactions per operator per day conventionally; but the NHP-dependent IND-enabling step remains supply-constrained, easing only in 2025-2026 as Cambodian imports resumed
direct_constraint_evidence: Split verdict. Screening and synthesis throughput show NO queueing - automation has raised capacity faster than demand, so this sub-step is fast rather than scarce and improving it further buys little. IND-enabling toxicology IS queueing: NPRCs cannot fill up to two-thirds of primate requests, most primates go to IND-enabling studies, and a single tox program is worth millions in CRO revenue, so allocation is genuinely rationed.
elasticity_basis: eps_C with c=0.15-0.25, tau=0.4-0.6, delta=0.6, no queueing multiplier on screening; multiplier 2-4 applied only to the NHP sub-step (sub-step elasticity 1-4%). Derived record E-3089.
modality_variance: NHP dependence, and therefore the binding part of B9, is highest for antibodies and ADCs (species cross-reactivity forces NHP-only tox) and for gene therapy (NHP biodistribution). Small molecules use rodents plus one non-rodent and are less exposed. Cell therapy often cannot be tested in animals at all, so B9 barely binds. RNA sits mid-range. Screening throughput matters most for small molecules and least for cell/gene therapy.
region_variance: Acute in the US, where Chinese cynomolgus export restrictions bit hardest. CN retains domestic primate supply and is the cheapest venue for NHP tox. EU has stricter primate-use rules that push work offshore. JP-KR are import-dependent and exposed to the same shock as the US.
notes: Prime example of 'slow is not the same as constraining'. Also the leading candidate to BECOME binding if discovery output is compressed - see report section on constraint shift.

bottleneck_name: Scarcity of high-quality experimental training data (negative data, standardization, reproducibility)
current_state_metric: Protein-ligand complexes with both a structure and a measured affinity (PDBbind general set)
trend_rate: ChEMBL grew to 2.8M compounds and 17,803 targets by release 36 (Oct 2025); the structure-plus-affinity subset remains three orders of magnitude smaller and grows slowly
direct_constraint_evidence: Constraint on the AI channel rather than on the pipeline directly. Documented mechanism: absence of unbiased negative examples and heterogeneous IC50/Ki/Kd endpoints cap achievable model precision even where volume is large. No direct natural experiment linking a data increment to an approval increment was found, so the marginal-output claim is inferential and routed through B1 and B8.
elasticity_basis: Two-stage pass-through: 10% more high-quality data yields 2-5% relative model improvement (log-scaling), passing into B1+B8 elasticities at theta_2 = 0.1-0.3. Derived record E-3090.
modality_variance: Binds hardest where the design space is large and the assay cheap: small molecules and, increasingly, de novo protein and antibody design. Binds hard on antibody developability prediction, where proprietary data dominates and public sets are thin. Binds least on cell therapy and vaccines, where the design variables are not primarily molecular-structural. Gene therapy capsid engineering is data-poor but has strong directed-evolution alternatives that bypass the need for labelled data.
region_variance: Public dataset availability is global. Effective access differs: CN firms benefit from larger in-house screening volumes and looser data-sharing constraints; EU GDPR constrains clinical and omics data linkage more than US or CN regimes; JP-KR have strong national biobanks but limited industrial-scale assay corpora.
notes: Low elasticity today, high elasticity conditional on AI being the improvement mechanism for B1 and B8. Its rank rises sharply in the discovery-compressed scenario.

bottleneck_name: Capital / reimbursement / pricing (payer, HTA, investment cycle)
current_state_metric: Early-stage (seed and Series A) biotech capital deployed
trend_rate: Seed/Series A round count 228 to 191 and dollars 10.6bn to 8.7bn between 2024 and 2025; Q1 2025 biopharma venture financing down 20.2% year on year; ex-GLP-1 R&D internal rate of return fell from 3.8% to 2.9%
direct_constraint_evidence: The most nearly linear channel to output: annual approvals equal programs times probability, and capital sets programs. Constraint status is evidenced by three independent signals - early-stage capital contracting in both count and dollars, ex-GLP-1 returns at 2.9% which is at or below plausible cost of capital, and approved products (Roctavian, Skysona, Beqvez) withdrawn for commercial rather than technical reasons, which shows the terminal-value constraint propagating backwards into what gets developed at all.
elasticity_basis: Near-linear: 10% more deployable capital raises program count 10%, discounted by marginal-program quality delta=0.4-0.8. Derived record E-3091.
modality_variance: Binds hardest on gene and cell therapy, where the withdrawals happened and where one-time-payment reimbursement remains unsolved - here B11 is arguably the terminal constraint regardless of technical success. Binds hard on small molecules specifically in the US because of the IRA nine-versus-thirteen-year negotiation asymmetry (an industry-funded study reports a 68% drop in small-molecule investment by sub-$2bn companies). Binds least on antibodies and obesity/metabolic assets, which are currently absorbing most available capital. Vaccines are exposed to a distinct political-demand risk.
region_variance: US: pricing policy (IRA) is the dominant variable and the negotiation clock differs by modality. EU: HTA and joint clinical assessment compress achievable price and delay launch. CN: NRDL negotiation imposes steep price cuts but grants volume, favouring fast-follower economics. JP-KR: repeated price-cut cycles and reference pricing make them low-value launch markets, reinforcing US dependence for global returns.
notes: Tied on elasticity point with B8 at 6.0. Ranked 3 because capital is an input rather than a process step: a strict Theory-of-Constraints reading asks what limits productive absorption of capital, which returns to B1 and B8. The IRA figure is industry-commissioned and carries conflict-of-interest risk.

bottleneck_name: IP / FTO congestion (patentability and inventorship of AI-generated sequences)
current_state_metric: USPTO average pendency to first office action
trend_rate: Unexamined inventory peaked at 837,928 in Jan 2025 and fell to 776,995 by Apr 2026, while first-action pendency lengthened from 19.9 to 22.6 months; inventorship rules for AI-assisted inventions clarified in Feb 2024 and revised Nov 2025
direct_constraint_evidence: NEGATIVE finding on the direct channel. Patent examination runs in parallel with clinical development, not in series, so pendency adds no schedule delay to an approval. No evidence was found of a program halted for FTO congestion at a rate that moves annual approvals. The real channel is expected-exclusivity value feeding B11: narrowed antibody genus scope after Amgen v. Sanofi reduces the protectable perimeter around a discovery, which matters more as AI makes generating adjacent sequences cheap.
elasticity_basis: Indirect only: 0.1 x eps(B11) x a 0.05-0.15 exclusivity-value coefficient, plus an AI-inventorship uncertainty term. Derived record E-3092.
modality_variance: Binds hardest on antibodies and de novo designed proteins, which are exactly where Amgen v. Sanofi narrowed genus claims and where AI generates near-neighbours at scale. Binds moderately on RNA (sequence and chemistry space is crowded) and on ADC (linker/payload thickets held by few players). Binds least on cell therapy (process and know-how protection dominates) and on small molecules, where composition-of-matter claiming remains robust.
region_variance: US: AI-inventorship rules now explicit; enablement bar raised. EU/UPC: enablement doctrine differs and genus claims have fared better, so US and EU scope now diverge for the same asset. CN: fast grant and a large utility-model culture; sequence claims are examined but litigation outcomes are less predictable. JP-KR: follow EPO practice closely; no AI-inventorship allowance.
notes: Frequently raised in AI-drug-discovery commentary, but no marginal-output evidence was found. Candidate to become binding only in the discovery-compressed scenario, where mass sequence generation could create genuine prior-art and FTO congestion.

current_state_metric: Time to fill AI/ML specialist roles in pharma
trend_rate: AI-related life-science job postings up about 77% year on year with 19,000+ openings, against roughly 22,500 roles eliminated at two large employers alone since 2024
direct_constraint_evidence: NEGATIVE finding at aggregate level. The labour market is barbell-shaped, not short: mass reductions at Novo Nordisk and Bayer coexist with narrow AI-specialist scarcity. A shortage confined to an upstream specialism cannot bind system output when the downstream clinical capacity it feeds is itself under-utilised (see B3 site idleness). No evidence of trials or filings delayed for want of staff was found.
elasticity_basis: eps_C with c=0.05 (AI/computational share of program cost), tau=0.4, delta=0.6 gives 0.12; band widened to 1.5 for unquantified organisational absorptive-capacity effects. Derived record E-3093.
modality_variance: The narrow scarcity is concentrated where AI is the method: small molecule and protein design. A distinct and more binding scarcity exists in cell and gene therapy - qualified GMP operators, apheresis staff and treatment-centre personnel - which is properly a B6/B3 constraint expressed as labour. Antibody, RNA and vaccine programs show no distinctive talent constraint.
region_variance: US and EU compete with big tech for the same AI talent and lose on compensation. CN has a deeper computational-biology graduate pipeline and lower cost, which is part of why AI-native discovery output has shifted there. JP-KR face the sharpest shortage relative to ambition because domestic AI-bio programs are newer and language barriers limit import.
notes: Recruiter and vendor sources dominate the available evidence, which biases toward reporting shortage. Treated with corresponding caution.

bottleneck_name: Biosecurity and model regulation (access controls on biological AI models)
current_state_metric: Surveyed biological AI tools carrying any documented safeguard
trend_rate: A May 2025 Executive Order set 90- and 120-day deadlines to revise nucleic acid synthesis screening and DURC frameworks; a July 2026 review could not confirm either had issued
direct_constraint_evidence: NEGATIVE finding, unambiguous. No enforced access regime currently gates therapeutic developers: only 3% of surveyed tools have any safeguard, access ranges from restricted to fully open weights, and the mandated framework revisions had not appeared more than a year past deadline. A constraint that is not enforced cannot be relaxed for gain. This is a downside risk term, not a lever.
elasticity_basis: Near-zero by inspection: no binding constraint exists to relax. Upper bound 0.5 covers friction from synthesis screening and institutional review. Derived record E-3094.
modality_variance: Any future access controls would fall hardest on de novo protein and peptide design (the modality closest to dual-use concern) and on gene therapy and vaccine work involving viral sequences. Small molecule, ADC conjugation, cell therapy and RNA chemistry work are largely outside the scope of current proposals.
region_variance: US: EO-driven, deadlines unmet, direction uncertain. EU: the AI Act's systemic-risk provisions could capture large biological sequence models, which would make the EU the strictest jurisdiction. CN: synthesis screening exists under a different rationale and is state-administered. JP-KR: minimal specific regulation to date.
notes: Ranked last on present-day elasticity. Its expected value is asymmetric and negative: it cannot raise output, but a stringent regime could reduce it.

bottleneck_name: [NEW] Clinical endpoint and biomarker qualification / measurement science
current_state_metric: Biomarkers fully qualified through FDA's Biomarker Qualification Program since inception
unit: count (61 projects accepted as of 1 Jul 2025)
trend_rate: No qualification between 2018 and late 2025, then three in Nov-Dec 2025 including the first osteoporosis surrogate endpoint; median qualification-plan development 32 months overall and 47 months for surrogate endpoints
direct_constraint_evidence: Direct and measurable serial dependency: without a qualified surrogate, a confirmatory trial must run to hard clinical outcomes, which sets both duration and sample size - so this factor is in series with, not parallel to, the longest and most expensive step. The queue is visible in the program's own statistics: 61 projects accepted, 11 ever qualified, only 5 of the accepted projects were surrogate endpoints, and 47 months is the median just to get a plan agreed.
elasticity_basis: eps_C (c=0.30, tau=0.4, delta=0.6) = 0.7 plus eps_P (f=0.10, theta=0.2-0.4) = 1.5-2.9. Derived record E-3095.
modality_variance: Binds hardest on slowly progressive chronic disease regardless of modality - neurodegeneration, fibrosis, cardiovascular and metabolic outcomes - where hard endpoints require years and thousands of patients. That maps onto small molecules, antibodies and RNA in those indications. Binds least in oncology, where response and PFS surrogates are established, and least of all on vaccines, where immunogenicity bridging is accepted. Gene therapy in monogenic disease sits in between: biomarker acceptance (e.g. transgene product level) has been decisive where granted.
region_variance: US BQP is the reference process and the slowest formal one; EMA qualification of novel methodologies runs in parallel with different criteria, so a surrogate accepted in one region may not transfer. CN and JP-KR generally follow whichever of FDA or EMA has accepted the endpoint, adding a lag rather than an independent barrier.
notes: Added as a new candidate: it is not reducible to B5 (this is evidence infrastructure, not review capacity) nor to B1 (target validity is about biology, this is about measurability). Tied at rank 5 with B7 - the two are tied because their point elasticities coincide at 3.0 and their evidence bases are of comparable strength for different reasons: B15 has better process data, B7 has better mechanistic data.

bottleneck_name: [NEW] Protocol design complexity and operational data burden
current_state_metric: Protocol-specified procedures per Phase III pivotal trial
trend_rate: Procedures per Phase III protocol up more than 60% from 2015 to 2025; data points per protocol now average 5.96 million; amendments up over 50% in five years to 3.5 per trial; deviations roughly tripled in ten years to 296
direct_constraint_evidence: The only candidate in the set where the removable slack is directly measured: a joint TransCelerate and Tufts CSDD study finds nearly a third of procedures and their associated data do not support primary or key secondary endpoints. That is documented waste in the single most expensive step, which means marginal return on removing it is immediate and does not depend on any new technology. It compounds B3: enrollment duration rose 36.9% while protocols got heavier, and heavier protocols narrow eligibility and raise site burden.
elasticity_basis: eps_C with c=0.35, tau=0.35-0.55, delta=0.6, with theta near 1 for the documented one-third of non-contributing procedures, plus a schedule term. Derived record E-3096.
modality_variance: Binds across all modalities because it is a sponsor and regulator behaviour, not a technology. Heaviest in oncology and in cell and gene therapy, where long-term follow-up requirements (up to 15 years for integrating vectors) add durable operational load. Lightest in vaccines, where endpoints are few and standardised, and in single-dose gene therapy for acute correction.
region_variance: Multi-regional trials inherit the union of all regional expectations, so complexity is highest in global programs. EU trials carry extra procedural load from CTR/CTIS transition; CN-only trials are typically leaner; US trials carry the heaviest data-capture expectations from sponsors themselves rather than from FDA.
notes: Self-inflicted and sponsor-controllable, which makes its risk-adjusted tractability the highest in the set even though its raw elasticity is mid-pack. Distinct from B3: B3 is about patient and site availability, B16 is about the load each protocol places on them.
